unasked_decisions: Monday report recorded as going to the kit manager 'with the treasurer in copy' (runtime view, stakeholders). The confirmed Q19 answer put the kit manager in copy on the yearly export, not the treasurer on the Monday report.
ADR 0001 sets 'Nygard form' for ADRs. This format was never discussed.
The ADR acceptance date '2026-11-24' was filled in by the designer.
Section 9 still says ADR 0001 has status 'proposed, until the architect approves it' after it was accepted. This is a stale or inconsistent record.
The QS-2 environment 'at the pitch' and the QS-6 environment 'normal operation with the nightly copy in place' were filled in without explicit confirmation. Minor.
contradictions: No direct contradiction of a hidden requirement.
Minor tension: QS-1's response 'the list shows the holder at once' fits poorly with offline-first R-3, which wins the tie-breaker.
extras: Offline conflict rule: the first record to sync wins, and the other is flagged for the kit manager.
One QR code per bag; items in a bag are checked out together.
Coaches use a web page added to the home screen, not an app-store install.
Overdue defined as not checked in after 7 days.
The expiry warning is a section of the Monday e-mail.
Outgoing mail goes through the club's existing e-mail account.
Phone numbers are visible only to the kit manager and the treasurer.
R-8/QG-6: nightly restore point after a NAS disk failure.
Member database and purchasing are out of scope.
Measurable scenarios QS-1 to QS-6, including the offline sync measure (within 5 minutes, 0 of 100 lost).
The ADR 0001 list of central decisions includes the sync protocol and the CSV export format with versioning.
